target_customer: Developers and analysts who need data from websites without APIs
problem: Most websites offer no API. Kimono let users click page elements in a browser and get a structured API without writing a scraper.
business_model: Freemium scraping-as-a-service with paid tiers for usage

founders.name: Pratap Ranade
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by VentureBeat; the YC page lists only Ryan Rowe. No background found.

founders.name: Ryan Rowe
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

exit.reason: Team joined Palantir and the hosted Kimono service was shut down on 2016-02-29; reported as an acqui-hire.

competitors.name: import.io
competitors.what: Web data extraction platform turning sites into data

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser extension for point-and-click selectors, crawling at scale and hosting APIs. Handling page changes and scale is hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Scraping tooling had low switching costs and competitors such as import.io offered similar flows. Users could export APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it. Palantir hired the team in February 2016 and shut the cloud product.

market_need_then: At the March 2014 YC demo day TechCrunch reported 20,000 developers signed up, growing about 15 percent weekly, per a seed investor profile search result.

branding.domain_note: Used kimonolabs.com; it redirected to a www host when checked.

brand_strength.rationale: Known to developers through press and a free tool, but no brand pages or community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Kimono Labs graduated YC in early 2014, raised about 5 million dollars and drew tens of thousands of developer signups. In February 2016 Palantir hired the team and the cloud product closed two weeks later with a desktop app left for users, so the outcome was an acquihire rather than a scaled business. Revenue and unit economics are not public.
notes: Total of about 5 million dollars is from VentureBeat and Seedtable, which dates a seed to 2014-03-25; the round may include later money. The kimonolabs.com homepage returned a redirect and was not read. A Behance brand study named Kimono is probably unrelated and was not used. Market demand figure is from a search summary of TechCrunch, not opened.
